issues.description: Method Rideable.messageOnRide: the problem statement (UML and task text) and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning a String (used as r.messageOnRide()). The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (takes an int parameter) and the implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int). This parameter mismatch is a breaking inconsistency: the template's call r.messageOnRide() will not compile against the solution's interface, and students will be unsure which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem statement and template by defining messageOnRide() with no parameters (String messageOnRide()) in Rideable and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg method (e.g. return "Riding on Pig <name>"). Alternatively, if a speed parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement UML, task description, and the template Main to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) consistently (and update example calls in Main to pass an int).
